title: Supported Python runtime
requirement: The package shall declare and test one supported Python runtime range and reject unsupported interpreters before normal execution.
rationale: A clear runtime contract prevents unsupported installations and false compatibility claims.
verification: Build and install release artifacts on every declared Python version; run help, version, initialization, and core lifecycle smoke tests.

title: Canonical files and rebuildable projections
requirement: Core Roadmap entities shall have one human-readable versioned Markdown and YAML representation under the repository-local .roadmap directory; databases indexes caches and analytics views shall be disposable projections.
rationale: Diffable portable canonical storage is the central product constraint while projections provide scalable queries.
verification: Round-trip representative entities and relations; delete corrupt and stale every projection; rebuild from files; compare semantic queries; verify canonical files always win disagreements.

title: Enforced architecture boundaries
requirement: Production modules shall follow one documented dependency direction enforced by a failing architecture test.
rationale: Enforced boundaries limit coupling and keep business rules testable.
verification: Add a focused policy test once the intended boundaries have a clean baseline; inject a known forbidden import and confirm the test fails.

title: Stable CLI contract
requirement: Documented commands options exit-code categories and machine-readable output shall remain compatible within a release line unless a breaking change is approved and documented; incidental human presentation and internal Python imports are not public by default.
rationale: Users and scripts depend on predictable declared behavior while internal architecture must remain evolvable.
verification: Exercise documented commands through installed-artifact tests; snapshot command schemas and structured output; require migration notes for approved breaks.

title: Owned validation and typed failures
requirement: Adapters shall validate representation Domain shall enforce single-aggregate invariants Application shall enforce contextual and cross-aggregate rules and inbound adapters shall translate typed failures to stable user-facing behavior.
rationale: One owner per rule prevents duplicated policy and framework leakage.
verification: Test valid boundary and invalid CLI configuration frontmatter CSV identifier date enum aggregate and cross-aggregate cases; assert failure category cause redaction exit behavior and no mutation.

title: Credential isolation and redaction
requirement: Authentication tokens and secrets shall use the system credential facility and shall not be serialized into repository data, exported output, telemetry, or logs.
rationale: Repository data is commonly committed and shared.
verification: Test storage, retrieval, deletion, missing backend, redaction, log capture, export, and error behavior on supported platforms.

title: Safe filesystem scope
requirement: All user-influenced paths and filenames shall be normalized, validated, and constrained to the intended project scope before file operations.
rationale: The CLI must prevent traversal, symlink escape, and unintended overwrite or deletion.
verification: Test traversal, symlink, invalid name, overwrite, permission, temporary-file, and archive edge cases; run the high-severity Bandit gate in CI and use targeted Semgrep reviews for security-sensitive changes.

title: Atomic and recoverable mutations
requirement: Every mutating use case shall run in an Application-owned unit of work implemented with workspace concurrency control atomic same-filesystem replacement conflict detection and deterministic recovery of interrupted multi-document commits.
rationale: Partial writes and concurrent edits can corrupt canonical project data.
verification: Inject interruption after every stage and test concurrent writers external edits disk-full permission loss stale locks rollback or roll-forward and projection failure on every supported OS.

title: Offline core operation
requirement: Core entity configuration requirement reporting health recovery and repository-inspection operations shall not require network access or a provider client.
rationale: Offline-first behavior is a product promise and Git owns repository transport.
verification: Run core journey tests with network access blocked; verify no Roadmap operation performs hidden fetch pull push or remote entity reconciliation.

title: Boundary failure isolation
requirement: Filesystem Git inspection credential telemetry database and external-command failures shall be translated by their adapters into bounded typed failures without corrupting canonical Roadmap data.
rationale: External mechanisms fail independently of local planning rules.
verification: Inject timeout permission malformed output stale data cancellation and process failures; verify typed causal errors redaction canonical readability and deterministic recovery.

title: Automated quality gate
requirement: Every code change shall pass formatting, linting, type, architecture, security, complexity, dead-code, package, documentation, and automated test gates defined in CI.
rationale: A visible failing gate keeps the repository maintainable and reviewable.
verification: Use negative gate tests to prove each policy fails when violated and verify required jobs complete on pull requests.

title: Cross-platform behavior
requirement: Supported CLI behavior and canonical data shall be portable across every declared operating system without platform-specific import or path failures.
rationale: The project targets developer workstations and repository portability.
verification: Run artifact and journey tests on the full OS matrix; include path, lock, credential, newline, encoding, shell, and executable discovery cases.

title: Deterministic structured output
requirement: JSON, CSV, and other machine-readable output shall be syntactically valid, deterministic for equivalent inputs, schema-versioned where persisted, and separated from diagnostics.
rationale: Reliable output enables shell pipelines, reporting, and interchange.
verification: Parse emitted formats; validate documented schemas; compare equivalent inputs; test nulls, Unicode, delimiters, errors, empty data, and stdout/stderr separation.

title: Structured observability
requirement: Logs audit events and optional telemetry shall provide correlation and diagnostic context without secrets changes to command results or a second store for canonical history.
rationale: Actionable diagnostics shorten recovery while Git history remains the audit source for committed roadmap state.
verification: Capture representative success failure retry and recovery diagnostics; verify severity correlation redaction disabled mode output isolation and no duplication of canonical content.

title: Documentation and release traceability
requirement: User-visible behavior changes shall update relevant documentation, requirements, migration guidance, and the Unreleased changelog.
rationale: Traceability keeps product claims, implementation, and release communication aligned.
verification: Review pull requests for requirement IDs, acceptance evidence, docs, changelog, migrations, and passing link/build checks.

title: Isolated distributable package
requirement: Release artifacts shall contain the Roadmap package and console entry point without runtime dependencies that shadow its import namespace.
rationale: The primary user journey begins with a working installed command.
verification: Build wheel and sdist in a clean job; inspect metadata; install each artifact without the source tree; run help, version, and import smoke tests.

title: Consistent command execution
requirement: Every command shall use common context discovery, error translation, confirmation, dry-run, and exit-code conventions.
rationale: Consistent mechanics make a broad CLI learnable and scriptable.
verification: Run contract tests across representative read, write, destructive, network, and repair commands; assert output channel and exit behavior.

title: Idempotent workspace initialization
requirement: Workspace discovery and initialization shall be idempotent, dry-runnable, template-aware, and transactional when existing data is present.
rationale: Initialization errors must not destroy the first user experience or prior project data.
verification: Test clean, existing, partial, forced, custom-name, custom-template, interactive, noninteractive, and interrupted initialization.

title: Versioned configuration
requirement: Roadmap configuration shall use a validated versioned schema with explicit defaults secret separation scoped reset and forward migration; Git remotes authentication and transport policy shall not be duplicated as Roadmap sync configuration.
rationale: Configuration drift affects every journey and can expose secrets.
verification: Round-trip supported settings; reject unknown or invalid values; test reset scopes environment overrides migrations redaction and absence of sync-backend credentials.

title: Stable identity and referential integrity
requirement: Every aggregate shall have a stable opaque Roadmap ID and every typed relationship shall use that ID and validate across visible closed archived indexed and externally referenced state.
rationale: Traceability and safe recovery depend on identity that is independent of names paths and providers.
verification: Test collisions rename reassignment close archive restore external references missing targets duplicate links stale indexes and cross-aggregate lookups.

title: Valid workflow and retention transitions
requirement: Workflow status and retention lifecycle shall be separate explicit state machines with validated transitions reasons timestamps and idempotent behavior; archive shall not replace workflow status or change canonical path.
rationale: Conflating completion retention and storage location corrupts history and query meaning.
verification: Exhaustively test permitted and rejected close reopen archive restore and purge transitions repeated events derived progress visibility stable paths and relationship resolution.

title: Validated dependency graphs
requirement: Dependency relations shall prevent missing targets self-links duplicates and prohibited cycles and shall expose deterministic traversal and critical-path analysis across every retained lifecycle state.
rationale: Invalid graphs make scheduling and execution unreliable.
verification: Use property and example tests for graph mutation cycles disconnected nodes archived targets critical paths and large graphs.

title: Durable comments and audit history
requirement: Comments governed changes lifecycle events and supersession events shall retain stable authorship timestamps targets and history while committed content history remains inspectable through Git.
rationale: Context and accountability must survive handoff repository history and archive transitions.
verification: Round-trip create edit close archive restore purge corruption and migration cases; verify authorship ordering redaction stable targets and Git-visible canonical diffs.

title: Derived planning aggregates
requirement: Project milestone board daily and requirement coverage views shall derive counts and progress from canonical linked entities using one documented Application-owned calculation policy.
rationale: Duplicated or stale progress erodes planning trust.
verification: Reconcile aggregates after create reassignment transition archive restore projection rebuild and manual file edit; test empty overdue partial and stale-index states.

title: Safe Git command boundary
requirement: Git operations shall use bounded argument arrays, explicit repository scope, timeouts, cancellation, and translated errors without shell injection.
rationale: Git is both a core integration and an external failure boundary.
verification: Test dirty trees, missing Git, nested repositories, unusual paths, timeouts, command failure, branch collisions, and cancellation.

title: Reversible Git-hook integration
requirement: Roadmap-managed Git hooks shall be idempotent, composable with existing hooks, identifiable, configurable, and removable without deleting user content.
rationale: Hook installation modifies developer workflows and must be reversible.
verification: Test install/status/config/uninstall with absent, existing, chained, damaged, and repeated hook states on supported platforms.

title: Deterministic commit reference parsing
requirement: Commit parsing shall recognize only documented unambiguous references and apply idempotent mapped transitions.
rationale: False positives can change work state from ordinary commit prose.
verification: Use a table of valid, invalid, ambiguous, repeated, Unicode, multiline, revert, merge, and unknown-ID messages.

title: Git-owned synchronization boundary
requirement: Roadmap shall treat canonical repository files as its only synchronized state and shall not implement provider backends baselines three-way entity reconciliation or implicit fetch pull merge rebase or push operations.
rationale: One synchronization authority avoids a second distributed-state protocol.
verification: Run collaboration journeys with standard Git and blocked application network access; assert no Roadmap sync configuration checkpoint remote mapping or hidden transport is required.

title: Rebuildable derived projections
requirement: Every database index cache analytics table and materialized view shall be derivable from canonical files detect stale or incompatible state and rebuild idempotently without changing canonical content.
rationale: Query performance must not create a competing source of truth.
verification: Delete corrupt truncate age and schema-mismatch every projection; rebuild repeatedly; compare query results and canonical file digests before and after.

title: Stable lifecycle storage
requirement: Canonical entity paths shall derive from stable Roadmap identity and shall not change when title milestone assignment workflow status or archive visibility changes.
rationale: Mutable business state must not be encoded as a storage address or query index.
verification: Test rename reassignment close reopen archive restore and projection rebuild; assert one stable canonical path no duplicates Git-visible content-only changes and retained ID lookup.

title: Explicit external references
requirement: External URLs and identifiers shall be ordinary optional references that never replace Roadmap identity trigger network access or create baseline mapping and reconciliation state.
rationale: External context can be useful without introducing a second writable source.
verification: Round-trip add edit remove missing malformed duplicate and archived-reference cases; assert stable Roadmap identity no network calls and no provider-specific domain dependency.

title: Versioned export and report schemas
requirement: Export and report formats shall have documented fields, stable identifiers, deterministic ordering, safe overwrite behavior, and schema versions where compatibility requires them.
rationale: Exports become downstream interfaces and backup inputs.
verification: Golden-file and parser tests shall cover filters, Unicode, nulls, empty sets, quoting, column selection, schema changes, and file collisions.

title: Safe diagnostics and repair
requirement: Health, integrity, cleanup, and repair operations shall separate detection from mutation and provide exact findings, stable severity, dry-run, confirmation, recovery, and post-check evidence.
rationale: Automated repair is destructive unless its scope and result are auditable.
verification: Test each detector/fixer pair with healthy, damaged, ambiguous, permission-denied, partial-failure, dry-run, and repeated execution cases.

title: Backup, lifecycle, and recovery integrity
requirement: Backup archive restore purge and transaction-recovery operations shall preserve stable identity path relationships metadata and recoverability through atomic scoped changes.
rationale: Recovery features must be more trustworthy than the failure they address.
verification: Run deterministic round-trip and failure-injection tests for all entities nested relations collisions interrupted commits visibility transitions retention purge manual edits and post-recovery health checks.

title: Versioned data migration
requirement: Every canonical schema shall declare a version and provide explicit idempotent forward migration with preflight recovery guidance and unsupported-future-version rejection; projection schemas shall be rebuildable instead of migrated as authority.
rationale: Long-lived repository data outlives individual CLI releases.
verification: Test each supported source version repeated migration partial failure future-version rejection stable IDs paths archived metadata unknown-field preservation projection rebuild and semantic round-trip.

title: Measured performance envelope
requirement: Interactive and batch journeys shall have documented dataset-size and latency targets and shall avoid unbounded memory filesystem parsing and Git work; normal filtered queries shall use rebuildable projections where measurement justifies them.
rationale: Large retained and archived histories must remain predictable for the stated small-team audience.
verification: Benchmark list lookup daily board health dependency projection rebuild export and coverage journeys at defined visible closed and archived entity counts; fail on material regressions.

title: Requirement artifact schema
requirement: User and technical requirements shall share a versioned envelope and enforce type-specific fields, stable IDs, lifecycle values, priority, ownership, acceptance or verification criteria, and timestamps.
rationale: A small coherent schema enables governance without heavyweight tooling.
verification: Validate minimum, complete, boundary, invalid, and unknown-field artifacts for both types and round-trip semantic equality.

title: Requirement repository
requirement: Requirement files shall use repository interfaces that support create, read, update, list, archive, supersede, and transaction-safe import without coupling the domain to CLI or remote adapters.
rationale: Requirements need the same file-first guarantees as other core entities.
verification: Run repository contract tests across file layout, manual edits, duplicates, archive, supersession, failure rollback, and cross-platform paths.

title: Governed requirement lifecycle
requirement: Requirement transitions shall enforce governance rules, record reasons and actors, require evidence for Verified, and avoid silently deriving governed decisions from issue state.
rationale: Requirements are decisions, not task status aliases.
verification: Test every transition, role assumption, accepted-content change, verification prerequisite, reopen, defer, reject, and roadmap eligibility rule.

title: Typed traceability graph
requirement: Requirement relationships shall use an extensible typed graph with target-type validation, bidirectional discovery, duplicate prevention, and cycle policies.
rationale: Typed traceability separates intent, implementation, planning, and evidence.
verification: Test every relation type, missing and archived targets, duplicate edges, prohibited cycles, unlinking, supersession, migration, and graph traversal.

title: Transactional requirement CSV interchange
requirement: Requirement CSV export and import shall be deterministic, round-trip supported fields, validate the whole change set, preview conflicts, and commit atomically.
rationale: CSV is useful for bulk review but must not become a divergent source of truth.
verification: Export canonical fixtures, re-import unchanged and modified copies, inject invalid and conflicting rows, and verify dry-run and rollback behavior.

title: Traceability and coverage queries
requirement: Coverage calculations shall use explicit eligible populations and relations and shall expose missing work, evidence, dependencies, and orphan implementation by journey, priority, milestone, and release.
rationale: Coverage must reveal gaps rather than reward record count.
verification: Reconcile query results to canonical fixtures for empty, partial, complete, archived, superseded, and broken graphs; test structured output.

title: Verification evidence and audit
requirement: Verification evidence shall record evidence type, stable location or digest, result, reviewer, time, and applicability and shall remain auditable after requirement evolution.
rationale: A Verified label without evidence provides false assurance.
verification: Test missing, passing, failing, stale, superseded, external, and deleted evidence and verify lifecycle reconciliation without history loss.

title: Requirement schema migration
requirement: Requirement artifacts and relations shall participate in versioned workspace migration without losing stable IDs, history, evidence, or supersession links.
rationale: Requirements are intended to outlive implementation work and releases.
verification: Migrate every supported requirement schema fixture, repeat migrations, interrupt and resume, reject future schemas, and compare semantic graphs before and after.
